hypothesis: Pigment-network states are repeatedly reachable through regulatory/flux changes
chun_result_basis: 8/8 independent mechanistic clusters show regulatory/flux evidence; 6/6 red-direction clusters show higher anthocyanin; no positive structural-loss requirement in informative clusters
remaining_test: common raw-RNAseq module effect-size meta-analysis
claim_boundary: supports recurrent accessibility, not a natural mechanism frequency

hypothesis: Anthocyanin-like red/pink floral state generally enables colder climatic niche expansion in Camellia
chun_result_basis: original exact 50-species A-W thermal tests were null; after the strongest current S3 provenance sensitivity BIO6 median A-W=-0.583 C P=0.509, q05=-0.484 C P=0.553, q01=-1.326 C P=0.227 and min=-1.547 C P=0.308. Fixed-n20 occurrence resampling intervals for q05/min/lower20 all cross zero; section-relative niche displacement is also null (P=0.287 without tail; P=0.269 with provenance-clean tail).
remaining_test: future work should be restricted to validated branch-specific conditional effects and latent pigment axes
claim_boundary: do not retain visible A/red as a genus-wide cold-enabler hypothesis

hypothesis: Anthocyanin deployment facilitates cold/UV adaptation only in particular lineages or ecological contexts
chun_result_basis: macro literature contains support/null/counterexample units; genus-wide visible A-W thermal tests remain null after provenance/estimator checks; intermediate tail significance appeared and disappeared as provenance gates changed
remaining_test: validated primary nuclear-tree branch-event tests using uncertain ecological boundaries and mechanistic pigment/spectral states rather than visible hue
claim_boundary: plausible only conditionally; every candidate boundary event must first pass provenance and estimator-uncertainty gates

hypothesis: Yellow state is unusually historically/geographically constrained
chun_result_basis: Fan Data S1 species analysis: Y 22/22 confined to South China/Southwest China/Vietnam versus non-Y 64/84; one-sided Fisher P=0.00552; A vs W geography P=1.0; current climate boundary sample has only two Y taxa and both have n=5
remaining_test: nuclear-tree ancestral range/transition reconstruction plus expanded occurrence/pigment evidence
claim_boundary: supports geographic/historical constraint, not a yellow thermal optimum; current climate-boundary data are inadequate for Y

hypothesis: Red/pink anthocyanin-like state expands beyond southern ancestral belt more readily than white
chun_result_basis: Fan Data S1 species geography: A 21/28 south-only vs W 43/56; OR=0.907, Fisher P=1.0
remaining_test: nuclear-tree historical range reconstruction
claim_boundary: A and W are indistinguishable in this source-geography contrast

hypothesis: Visible flower-colour states are strongly structured by lineage/history rather than being distributed independently across Camellia
chun_result_basis: Fan Data S1 deterministic species table excluding non-section Vietnam rows: 98 species across 17 traditional sections; section×colour Pearson chi2=178.646, Cramer's V=0.955, 100000-shuffle permutation P<1e-5; e.g. sect. Camellia 22/23 A, sect. Chrysantha 13/13 Y, sect. Thea 14/14 W
remaining_test: replace traditional-section proxy with admitted nuclear-tree phylogenetic signal / transition model
claim_boundary: traditional sections are not assumed monophyletic; the former section×cold-tail association is explicitly excluded because invalid extreme occurrences drove it

hypothesis: Molecular accessibility generates variants while ecology/history filters which states persist macroevolutionarily
chun_result_basis: strong micro recurrence contrasts with weak visible-hue macro thermal effects; yellow geography and colour-history structure are strong; occurrence audits show ecological boundaries need an observation layer before filtering can be inferred
remaining_test: latent pigment/sensory state + uncertain environmental/pollinator boundaries + primary-tree transition/event model
claim_boundary: supported as synthesis pattern; causal filters and event ordering are not yet separated

hypothesis: The exact pigment-network nodes labile within development/cultivars are preferentially reused on macroevolutionary colour-transition branches
chun_result_basis: cross-scale accessibility pattern motivates this but macro branch gene assignments are not yet available
remaining_test: primary nuclear tree + transition mapping + raw RNAseq/common ortholog node enrichment
claim_boundary: not yet demonstrated

hypothesis: Pollinator sensory environment helps determine which accessible pigment/spectral states persist
chun_result_basis: species-level pollination evidence is heterogeneous; same visible red can be bird-associated or insect-associated
remaining_test: phylogenetic analysis on spectrum/UV, nectar, season and effective pollination using latent pigment state
claim_boundary: do not infer from human colour categories alone

hypothesis: Anthocyanin-like A lineages occupy narrower thermal breadth than W lineages
chun_result_basis: OpenTree synthetic topology + Grafen BM-PGLS previously gave BIO1 IQR A-W=-1.17 C P=0.000233 while raw species-label tests were non-significant; the synthetic-tree result predates the full provenance audit
remaining_test: rerun only after full provenance cleaning and preferably on primary dated nuclear tree
claim_boundary: do not promote from topology-only/pre-provenance sensitivity

hypothesis: Human-visible W/A/Y states merge distinct biochemical, sensory and ecological states and therefore lose macroevolutionarily relevant information
chun_result_basis: red C. japonica and red C. rusticana have different pollination/sensory regimes; mechanistic ledger shows multiple regulatory/flux routes to superficially similar less-red/white states; yellow C. nitidissima combines flavonol and carotenoid deployment
remaining_test: expand species latent pigment/spectral matrix and compare predictive/phylogenetic fit against W/A/Y on primary nuclear trees
claim_boundary: supports visible hue as a lossy deterministic proxy, not yet superiority of one latent representation

hypothesis: White is often an accessible retained-pathway reservoir/bridge rather than a terminal pigment-loss state
chun_result_basis: published visible root is white and extant white systems retain flavonoid/pathway activity; raw exact-subset breadth W=9/10 sections is not unusually broad after state-count control: expected breadth=9.12673 P=0.651 and entropy P=0.413
remaining_test: nuclear-tree stochastic maps with root/state-frequency/sampling controls plus pathway-retention evidence on W->coloured branches
claim_boundary: do not use broad section occupancy as evidence for a white hub; reservoir/bridge status requires excess transition centrality and retained machinery

hypothesis: Ecological function can change while coarse visible hue remains similar
chun_result_basis: red C. japonica is bird-associated whereas red C. rusticana is insect/bee-associated with distinct UV/fluorescence cues; this sensory/pollination contrast does not depend on GBIF thermal tails
remaining_test: expand spectra/UV/pollinator matrix across independent same-hue species pairs
claim_boundary: one within-genus case establishes non-uniqueness of hue-to-function mapping, not its genus-wide frequency

hypothesis: Extreme climatic range limits are generated by rare lineage-specific boundary shifts rather than broad visible-colour regimes
chun_result_basis: C. rhytidocarpa and C. tuberculata shared two implausible extreme coordinates; removing them shifts q05 by +15.53 and +16.815 C and destroys the apparent section signal. Wider provenance cleaning also removes intermediate deep-tail A-W significance.
remaining_test: search for candidate branch-edge events only after provenance/range and estimator validation
claim_boundary: reject Tuberculatae as evidence for a biological cold-edge innovation; true rare edge events may exist elsewhere

hypothesis: Occurrence provenance can dominate lower-tail climatic niche inference in Camellia
chun_result_basis: a BOLD country-centroid coordinate occurs in 27 exact taxa; other area/generic coordinates and hard range conflicts are present. Staged S0-S3 cleaning changes A-W q01/min from null to significant at intermediate stages and back to null under the stronger gate; Tuberculatae q05 shifts by >15 C after two records/taxon are removed.
remaining_test: automate provenance/range audits for all environmental axes and candidate branch edges
claim_boundary: demonstrated across the current 50-species dataset; exact prevalence of all error modes remains incomplete

hypothesis: Lower-tail niche estimators are taxon-specific uncertain observations whose stability depends on occurrence sample size
chun_result_basis: after S3 cleaning, retained n versus max absolute leave-one-record-out q05 change has Spearman rho=-0.52047 P=0.0001069; median max change is 0.610 C at n=5-9, 0.670 C at n=10-19 and 0.285 C at n>=20
remaining_test: add locality-block bootstrap and alternative quantile/tail estimators; propagate species-level boundary uncertainty into phylogenetic model
claim_boundary: q05 is not rejected, but must not be treated as an error-free species trait

hypothesis: Occurrence-derived climatic boundary events require a stronger evidence layer than niche centroids before macroevolutionary lead/lag inference
chun_result_basis: country-only/standard geospatial filtering admitted records that generated false extreme boundaries; provenance + range plausibility + coordinate reuse + leverage checks reverse the Tuberculatae interpretation
remaining_test: apply gate to all future boundary events and retain provenance metadata in artifacts
claim_boundary: an analysis can be statistically correct but biologically invalid if the environmental event itself is artefactual

hypothesis: Hard boundary-quality filtering can create a non-random evolutionary-state/lineage sample
chun_result_basis: provisional n>=20 and max LOO q05<=1 C gate retains 26/50 taxa (A 10/14, W 16/34, Y 0/2); stronger gate retains 17/50 and Y 0/2. A-W pass-rate difference is not significant (Fisher P=0.202), so colour-dependent ascertainment is not established; complete loss of current Y boundary taxa demonstrates state-coverage distortion.
remaining_test: model evidence/admission probability by lineage, geography and data source; expand Y occurrences before branch modelling
claim_boundary: diagnostic gate thresholds are not universal biological cutoffs; do not solve uncertainty by complete-case deletion alone

hypothesis: High molecular accessibility is filtered by lineage-specific permissivity so readily generated anthocyanin-like states become macro-persistent only in some historical/ecological backgrounds
chun_result_basis: micro layer shows 8/8 regulatory/flux recurrence and 6/6 red-direction anthocyanin recurrence, yet in exact 50-species screen A=14 taxa occupy only 2 traditional sections versus 6.59279 expected under 100000 state-label shuffles; breadth lower-tail P=0.00003 and entropy P<0.00001
remaining_test: primary nuclear stochastic mapping; test A gain/persistence concentration after branch opportunity/topology uncertainty are controlled
claim_boundary: traditional sections and climate subset are history proxies, not direct phylogenetic transition rates

hypothesis: Selection on flower-colour evolution acts more directly on biochemical/spectral latent phenotype than on human-visible W/A/Y hue
chun_result_basis: same-hue functional collisions plus weak provenance-clean visible-hue thermal models motivate this; current latent-state audit has pollinator 6/8 but UV/fluorescence 1/8 and carotenoid 1/8
remaining_test: fill spectral/UV and pigment-chemistry axes; compare latent-state versus W/A/Y predictive and phylogenetic models
claim_boundary: case evidence falsifies deterministic hue-to-function mapping but does not yet prove a particular latent model is superior

hypothesis: Adaptive pigment reactivation can be an ecological enabler or an ecological follower and the distinction is determined by branch-level temporal ordering
chun_result_basis: strong molecular accessibility coexists with null present-day visible A-W climate association, so cross-sectional correlation cannot identify whether environment/pollinator change or pigment reactivation came first
remaining_test: dated primary nuclear histories plus validated uncertain climate/light/pollinator events; compare environment-first, trait-first, pollinator-first and synchronous histories
claim_boundary: no Camellia branch-specific true reactivation has yet passed the historical + retention gate

hypothesis: Climate can select pigment re-deployment indirectly by altering pollinator reliability or seasonality
chun_result_basis: direct genus-wide red/cold mapping is unsupported while source-level C. petelotii shows weather-sensitive bee visitation and C. perpetua shows seasonal bird/bee weighting; same-red Camellia can target different pollinators
remaining_test: test climate/season -> pollinator regime -> latent pigment/spectral state against direct climate -> hue on dated branches
claim_boundary: plausible mediation model; current cases do not demonstrate macroevolutionary reactivation

hypothesis: Some pigment reactivations restore a previously useful signal when an ancestral-like ecological regime recurs rather than enabling a genuinely novel niche
chun_result_basis: generated by retained-pathway accessibility, same-hue functional variation in Camellia and empirical pollinator-associated colour regain outside Camellia
remaining_test: reconstruct ancestral and post-reactivation ecological regimes; compare ancestral-to-post-reactivation ecological distance against novel-niche alternatives
claim_boundary: general regain precedent exists outside Camellia; this mechanism is not yet demonstrated in Camellia

hypothesis: Both flower-colour state and ecological boundary are noisy observation layers; treating either as error-free overstates precision of macroevolutionary associations
chun_result_basis: predictor-side state aliasing is independently supported; response-side provenance/estimator uncertainty is independently supported. After S3, observed q05 A-W=-0.484 C; centered within-species occurrence-resampling diagnostic interval is [-1.390,+0.192] C and nested species+occurrence interval [-2.206,+1.140] C.
remaining_test: fit joint observation + phylogenetic event model with uncertainty on both sides
claim_boundary: supports changing model architecture; not yet a fitted latent phylogenetic result

hypothesis: Independent Camellia branches can follow different pigment-first, environment-first, pollinator-first, synchronous or independent histories
chun_result_basis: present-day cross-sectional visible-hue correlations are weak/null while molecular accessibility is recurrent, so one global association cannot identify a single evolutionary sequence
remaining_test: primary dated nuclear trees plus latent pigment and validated uncertain ecological/pollinator event histories
claim_boundary: event-order heterogeneity is a testable alternative, not yet demonstrated

hypothesis: The micro-to-macro test is limited by a mismatch between rich molecular/sensory information and sparse/uncertain species-level ecological-boundary evidence
chun_result_basis: latent pigment seed has structured missingness; boundary gates retain only 26/50 under mild diagnostic criteria and 17/50 under strong criteria; both current Y climate taxa have n=5 and fail the n-based boundary gate
remaining_test: expand species-level pigment/spectral and occurrence provenance evidence while modelling missingness rather than deleting incomplete taxa
claim_boundary: describes the current evidence architecture; not a biological evolutionary mechanism by itself

hypothesis: Coarse visible A/W hue contains little direct information about thermal niche evolution even though pigment-network deployment is mechanistically labile
chun_result_basis: raw, specimen-only and S3 provenance-clean A-W thermal tests are null; fixed-n resampling intervals cross zero; occurrence-observation uncertainty crosses zero; section-relative niche displacement P=0.287 without tail and P=0.269 with cleaned tail
remaining_test: repeat on primary nuclear trees and additional validated environmental/light axes; compare against latent pigment/sensory predictors
claim_boundary: supported only for current thermal/niche-displacement screens; does not imply visible hue is ecologically irrelevant to pollinators or other axes
